problem: Prior Navigation-by-Dialog-History (NDH) agents (seq-to-seq) concatenate the dialog history into one instruction and predict each action independently, ignoring visual history and the decisions made in earlier steps.
motivation: Vision-dialog navigation has a hierarchical trajectory (sub-trajectories per dialog round) and ambiguous oracle replies (e.g. 'go back') that need both dialog history and previously seen views to resolve. Visual dialog methods share one image across turns, so they do not handle temporally changing visual context.
key_idea: A Cross-modal Memory Network (CMN) with a language memory (multi-head attention over dialog history) and a visual memory (attention over current panorama conditioned on the previous step's cross-modal encoding), linked by language-to-vision and vision-to-language attention, to recall past navigation decisions.
insight: Both memories contribute: removing V-mem or L-mem lowers unseen GP from 2.97 to 2.52 / 2.64 (Tab. 2), and zeroing the previous cross-modal encoding (VL-mem) drops test GP from 2.95 to 2.54 or lower. Part of the gain comes from the panoramic-feature and panoramic-action baseline (VLN baseline 2.30 vs seq-to-seq 2.10 unseen), and the memory adds a further gain on top. Explicit temporal-order embedding gives comparable results to the implicit one.
method: Language features: GloVe embeddings + two-layer LSTM encode each dialog turn (Q+R) into d_t; history gives {d_i}.
L-mem: multi-head scaled dot-product attention of the current dialog over dialog history, with residual/LayerNorm/MLP; output d_ctx = concat(d_hat, d_t); can be stacked.
V-mem: previous-step cross-modal encoding e^vlm_{t,s-1} attends over the 36 panoramic ResNet-152 view features (2048-d) to give a memory-aware visual feature.
Cross-modal memory: language-to-vision attention (d_ctx over visual memories) gives e^vm, then vision-to-language attention over all dialog encodings gives e^vlm, forming a closed reasoning loop.
Action decoder: linear layers + softmax over panoramic candidate views (speaker-follower panoramic action space), trained with cross-entropy against shortest-path actions with student forcing.

setting.backbone: CMN: ResNet-152 features + GloVe + 2-layer LSTM + multi-head attention modules (trained from scratch, except pretrained CNN/GloVe)
setting.training_data: CVDN dataset (2050 dialogs, >7k trajectories, 83 MatterPort houses); RMSProp lr 1e-4, 20000 iterations, batch 60, student-forcing; ~2 GPU days on one 1080Ti
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views, ResNet-152 features) + dialog text history
setting.action_space: panoramic action space: discrete candidate viewpoints on nav graph
setting.privileged: none at test; training supervision uses shortest-path/oracle/mixed paths

numbers_note: CVDN is not in the canonical list, so I labelled the bench 'CVDN' (matching the CVDN entry in the list). Val-seen Tab. 2 also gives GP 7.05, OSR 65.2, SR 38.5, OPSR 76.4 (not entered in a separate row).
results: CMN gets GP 2.97 m / SR 22.8% on val-unseen, versus seq-to-seq 2.10 / 13.7% and the VLN baseline 2.30 / 19.7%. Test unseen mixed GP is 2.95, versus 2.35 for seq-to-seq.
limitations: Evaluated only on CVDN with pre-annotated dialogs (NDH); the agent does not ask questions itself.
Absolute unseen performance remains low (SR 22.8%) and the ablation of the memories is small on some metrics; the ablation-by-averaging design only partly disables memory.
Ablation numbers are best over validation checkpoints, so may be optimistic.
builds_on: Speaker-Follower panoramic action space (Fried et al.)
compares_to: Shortest path / random / vision-only / dialog-only baselines
